title: [all components] Reduce shared bundle size

labels.name: type: enhancement
labels.description: It’s an improvement, but we can’t make up our mind whether it's a bug fix or a new feature.

labels.name: scope: all components
labels.description: Widespread work has an impact on almost all components.

body:
## Summary

Reduces shared bundle cost across the popup, focus-management, and selector paths used by many Base UI components.

This PR keeps the measurable wins from the internal `tabbable` helper and the plain-vs-memoized selector split, trims shared utility code used across popup-heavy components, and avoids the broader unverified `@base-ui/utils/store/...` import-path churn so store consumers continue to use the standard barrel entrypoint.

## Changes

- Replace the external `tabbable` dependency with a smaller internal helper and add focused regression coverage for shadow DOM, `details`, hidden controls, radio groups, inert content, and embedded focusable elements.
- Split plain and memoized selector helpers so entrypoints that only need plain selectors do not pull memoized selector overhead.
- Remove redundant non-reactive Combobox store selector subscriptions.
- Simplify shared render, transition, animation, popup, and store utilities used across multiple components.

## Notes

- The latest published bundle bot result on this PR reports `@base-ui/react` down by `4.33 KB` parsed and `1.57 KB` gzip versus `master`.
- Latest targeted perf checks in exported production builds still favor the PR head on `combobox-perf` and `select-perf`, while a Chromium `100`-slider mount check is effectively flat versus `master`.
- Broader popup-route perf has been mixed rather than uniformly better, so this PR should be understood primarily as a shared bundle-size reduction with targeted runtime wins, not as an across-the-board popup perf improvement.
